lines.text: Past midnight, when the whole camp was asleep, Hask walked out alone into my fields.
He didn't know that someone was still awake to see him.
He knelt in the barley. He took off his glove. And he laid his bare hand flat on the earth.
Tamsin told me later what she saw that night. The ground lit up under his hand. Faint and pale, like frost. Except it was warm.
Warm. The whole field is warm. Gods above. The whole valley.
He went back to his tent and wrote a letter. Just one word, Tamsin said. She saw it over his shoulder before he sealed it.
Then he tied it to a white bird, and let it go. South. Toward the capital.
At that same moment, in the keep, I woke up so cold I couldn't breathe.
One of the threads was pulling north. Far north, into the Pale. And it hurt. Someone in Wren's party was bleeding.
My lord? I heard you shout.
Someone's hurt. In the Pale. I can feel it.
Then there's nothing to do tonight but trust her.
Bram was right. That was the worst part. Being a lord who can feel his people bleeding, and can't do a single thing about it.
And far above us, a white bird flew south, carrying one word that would change everything.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter twenty-two, coming soon.
